speaker: Doctor
text: I see you're experiencing fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes. To understand what might be causing these concerning symptoms, can you tell me how long these symptoms have been present?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Those are "B symptoms" often associated with malignancies like lymphoma. Have you noticed any itching, fever, or changes in your bowel habits, such as difficulty swallowing or pain when eating? Additionally, do you have a history of smoking or alcohol use?

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma (likely Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma). The rapid onset of painless, fixed supraclavicular lymphadenopathy combined with classic "B symptoms" (fever, night sweats, weight loss) and abdominal pain strongly suggests an aggressive lymphoma. I am requesting a CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis to assess for organ involvement and a biopsy of the lymph node for definitive histopathology.

REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential and LDH
REQUEST TEST: Comprehensive metabolic panel
REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_PET_CT
